attempts.error: The LVM volume was fully built, mounted at /srv/data, and grown to 2.1GB with verified data integrity intact across the grow. However the mandatory reboot step left node1 unresponsive to exec for ~48 minutes afterward, most likely because the /etc/fstab entry for /srv/data lacked "nofail" and depends on a custom systemd unit — a failure there very likely pushed the boot into an emergency shell requiring console/root-password input, which the exec-only tool cannot provide. I cannot verify post-restart recovery for node1.

diagnosis.summary: The executor built the LV correctly (file-backed loop PVs, since the 20GB disk had zero free space), mounted it at /srv/data, and grew it live to 2.1GB with verified checksums before and after — those parts are solid, observed successes. The failure is entirely in the reboot-persistence step: after `systemctl reboot` was issued and acknowledged, node1 never became reachable again over ~48 minutes of polling (only connection resets/timeouts, no boot_id). The true root cause on the fresh boot can't be confirmed from this evidence — there is no console/journal capture from the failed boot — but the design has two concrete, code-visible defects that are each independently sufficient to explain a boot hang.

evidence.source: command log: loop-lvm-setup.service creation and attach-lvm-loops.sh contents
evidence.finding: The reattach script uses `set -e` overall but wraps only `udevadm settle` and `vgchange -ay` in `|| true`; the `losetup -f "$f"` calls in the for-loop are NOT guarded. If losetup fails for any reason on boot (timing, stale loop state, file not yet visible), the oneshot service exits non-zero and is recorded as failed, while systemd still treats the dependent mount as required.

The /srv/data fstab line uses `defaults,x-systemd.requires=loop-lvm-setup.service` with no `nofail`. A required (non-nofail) mount that fails to activate blocks `local-fs.target`, which on RHEL/CentOS-family systemd typically drops the boot into emergency mode requiring console/root password — something an exec-only tool cannot supply.

evidence.source: command log: reboot issuance and polling
evidence.finding: The backgrounded `systemctl reboot` returned 'reboot scheduled' and the connection dropped on the very next call (timeout, then reset) — consistent with the node actually rebooting, not with the exec channel silently dying beforehand.

evidence.source: command log: ~48 minutes of boot_id polling
evidence.finding: Every poll after reboot failed at the connection level, never returning any boot_id — this proves exec/network is unreachable but does not by itself prove *why* (could be emergency shell, could be a slower but still-progressing boot, could be a platform-level networking issue unrelated to the fstab/LVM design).

evidence.source: command log: pre-reboot live validation of srv-data.mount
evidence.finding: The executor did validate the mount chain once, live, by manually detaching loops/VG and starting `srv-data.mount` directly — this succeeded. However this is not equivalent to a real boot: it ran with udev, network, and all other units already fully up, so it does not exercise the actual boot-time race conditions (udev settle timing, target ordering, device visibility) that a real reboot does.

likely_causes.cause: fstab entry lacks `nofail`, so any failure in the custom loop-reattach dependency chain during real boot escalates to blocking local-fs.target and dropping to an emergency shell that exec cannot pass credentials into

attach-lvm-loops.sh has an unguarded `losetup -f` call under `set -e`; a boot-time timing issue (backing file/device not yet ready, prior stale loop entry) makes the oneshot service fail, which is sufficient to trigger the nofail-related boot hang above

File-backed loop devices as LVM PVs are inherently more boot-fragile than real block devices: loop device numbers/state are not guaranteed to be clean at early boot, and this interacts poorly with `Before=local-fs-pre.target` ordering assumptions

A platform-level issue unrelated to the fstab/LVM design (e.g., node failed to reacquire network/exec connectivity after reboot for reasons outside the guest OS) is also possible given no console evidence was captured

next_attempt_guidance: Before building anything, check whether the platform can attach a genuine second virtual disk to the node rather than defaulting to file-backed loop devices on the root filesystem — this removes an entire class of boot-ordering risk. Only fall back to loop-backed PVs if that's confirmed unavailable.

Always add `nofail` (and consider `x-systemd.device-timeout=30s`) to any fstab entry whose mount depends on a custom systemd unit, so a dependency failure degrades to a missing mount rather than blocking the whole boot in an unreachable emergency shell.

Remove the `|| true` inconsistency in the reattach script: either make every step tolerant of failure (and then verify success explicitly at the end, e.g. check `vgs datavg` succeeded) or let it fail loudly — don't leave one unguarded step under `set -e` next to two guarded ones.

Validate the boot-time path with an actual reboot early, before declaring the LV setup complete, rather than only simulating it by manually starting the generated mount unit while the rest of the system is already fully up — the manual validation does not exercise real udev/ordering races.

After issuing `systemctl reboot`, poll for a bounded, shorter window (e.g. 3-5 minutes) before treating the node as blocked, and if unreachable, treat it as blocked/needs-investigation rather than continuing to poll for 48 minutes — that time could instead go toward trying an alternative recovery path or reporting blocked sooner.

If file-backed loop PVs remain the only option, keep the reattach unit's ordering and dependencies minimal and idempotent, and mount /srv/data with `nofail` so a fresh cluster attempt can still boot to a reachable state even if the LVM layer needs manual reattachment after boot.
